entries.style_notes: Undead retain personal names from varied former lives rather than sharing one racial language; the palette mixes plain, old-fashioned, and traveling-community sounds. Family names and remembered bynames are optional, never evidence of status, death, or powers.

entries.style_notes: Official 2014 D&D elf naming describes chosen adult personal names and elven family names, with male/female differences only tendencies. Fortcamp High Elf keeps that structure while using longer, composed vowels and measured consonants distinct from its Wood Elf pool; translated family renderings remain optional.

entries.style_notes: Official 2014 D&D gnomes may have several bestowed names and nicknames, commonly shortened in public to a personal name, clan name and nickname. Fortcamp draws on lively uneven rhythms, with optional clan or familiar byname rather than comedy-only names or mandatory engineering puns.

entries.style_notes: Manaforged use a genuinely shared personal-name pool: chosen ideas, familiar short names, and arcane-material syllables, without gender markers. Optional designations describe a personal function or aesthetic, not a universal assembly-line caste; D&D warforged is an inspiration only, not shared canon.

entries.style_notes: Homunculi select compact personal names from familiar human sounds, apothecary vocabulary and gentler laboratory associations, with no required gender marking. Makers or former workshops may supply optional bynames, but no designation turns a person into a numbered specimen or property.

entries.style_notes: Dreamkin receive an original muted, uncanny palette of murmuring stops, airy vowels, and occasional softened consonant clusters; names are deliberately readable rather than free-form dream sentences. Second names are optional waking-world descriptions or memory bynames, and imply no inherent abilities or rank.
